name: Reviews index filters and stack rows

pr.title: Filter the Reviews index by Open and Closed and draw each row like a stack row
pr.head: a01359c11e645e41ce8d7afd0bde65f61ca2af61

summary: A repository's Projector site has a Reviews index at reviews/: one row for each pull request that has a published summary, with its status and when its newest summary was published. The site's build writes the rows into site.json, and site.ts draws them in the browser. #213 grouped each stack's pull requests together on that page and hid merged and closed ones behind a Show merged and closed box.
This pull request reworks the page in four ways:

• Two filter boxes. Open and Closed, each with its count, replace the single box. A merged pull request counts as closed, and one whose state the build could not ask GitHub for counts as open. Only Open starts checked, and the address records any other choice as ?state=closed, ?state=open,closed, or ?state=, so a copied link opens the same list.
  • Rows drawn like the sidebar's stack. Each row is one cell holding the pull request's number in a narrow track and its title beside it, the way a summary page's sidebar lists the pull requests in its stack. Shared .srow, .snum, and .stitle rules in summary.css draw both.
  • Fewer columns. The Projects column goes, along with the projects list in site.json's reviews that only it read. Every column except the pull request's has a fixed width, so toggling a box never moves a column.
  • The pull request's title. Each row shows the pull request's title through pr_title, the same helper that titles its summary page, instead of the summary's name.
The review of this head found nothing to fix. The full test suite, the TypeScript check and build, project check, and both plugin validations pass.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Stack. Pull requests where each one's base branch is the head branch of the one beneath it. The index lists a stack's rows together, from the one on the default branch up.
  • Summary. The guided review page that project summary publish stores for a pull request. Each summary has a short name and the pull request's title.
  • site.json. The manifest the site's build writes. Its reviews list holds one row per pull request.
  • .srow. The CSS class for one pull request drawn as a number and a title, shared by the sidebar and the index.

groups.title: What site.json says about each review
groups.kicker: The build drops the projects list and titles each row as its page does.
intro: The site's build turns each pull request's newest summary into a row of site.json's reviews list with review_row. The browser reads only that list to draw the index.

The row loses projects, the names of the projects the pull request touches, because the Projects column was its only reader. A project page still lists its reviews, because the build computes each project's review numbers from its own entries, not from site.json's rows. The row's title now comes from pr_title, which falls back to the summary's name and then to #N when the pull request has no title.

checks.text: build_site still fills each project's reviews from the build's entries, which keep projects, so dropping it from the row leaves project pages unchanged. Checked by reading build_site and by test_a_review_links_to_the_projects_its_diff_changes_and_back and test_a_summary_can_name_a_project_its_diff_does_not_touch passing, which assert each project's reviews.

files.note: SiteReview loses its projects field to match the row.

groups.title: One pull request row for the sidebar and the index
groups.kicker: The sidebar's stack-row look moves into shared .srow, .snum, and .stitle rules.
intro: A summary page's sidebar lists every pull request in its stack, one row each: a small monospace number, then the title on the number's line, with a band behind the row on hover. Those rules were scoped to the sidebar as .prblock .stack li > a, so the index could not reuse them.

The pull request moves the row's look into three unscoped classes in summary.css, which every site page already loads. .srow is the grid, .snum the number, and .stitle the title, clamped to three lines. Sizes are now relative: the number track is 2.9em and the number 0.92em, which reproduce the sidebar's former 36px and 11.5px at its 12.5px font size. The sidebar keeps only its own margin and size in .prblock .stack .srow.

files.note: Adds the shared row rules and trims the sidebar's rules to size and margin.

checks.text: .srow has the low specificity of one class, so any rule naming an element and a class beats it. In the sidebar no .nav ol a or .nav .extra a rule reaches a stack row, because the stack is a ul outside .extra.

This rule had to go. At one class and one element it would beat .srow on display and padding and collapse every sidebar row to inline text. .prblock holds only the projects list and the stack list, so no other link depended on it. Checked by reading what renderPage puts in .prblock.

files.note: The sidebar's stack rows and project rows carry the srow class, and the current row gets it on its li.

checks.text: The current pull request's row is an li, not a link, so it takes srow itself to get the grid layout that .prblock .stack li.current used to set.

groups.title: The Reviews index
groups.kicker: Open and Closed boxes, a filter the address records, and rows drawn as .srow.
intro: showReviews draws the index. It reads which states to list from the address, draws one box for each state with its count, and redraws the list whenever a box changes. Each stack's rows still share one table body, so a stack stays together when a filter hides some of its layers.

Before this change one box toggled merged and closed pull requests on and off, and the choice did not survive a reload. Now a change writes the choice into the query with history.replaceState, leaving the path and the hash alone. The default, Open alone, writes no query at all, so the plain reviews/ link stays the default view.

The table uses table-layout: fixed with a colgroup. The Status and Updated columns get fixed widths, and the pull request column takes the rest and wraps its title. Rows inside a table body sit close together, and only the last row of each body draws a divider, so a stack reads as one block. At phone width the Updated column is hidden and the status may wrap.

files.note: showReviews draws the two boxes and keeps the address in step with them. reviewRow draws each row as an .srow.

checks.text: A pull request whose state the build could not ask GitHub for has no state, and stateOf lists it under Open, so it stays visible by default.

listedStates returns ['open'] with no state parameter and splits it on commas otherwise. An unknown value checks no box for it, so ?state=closed,bogus checks Closed alone. Checked by tracing it and by test_the_address_says_which_boxes_start_checked.

The handler rewrites only the query. Open alone writes none, and every other choice writes ?state= with the checked values. The site's own Reviews nav link still opens the default view, because the in-site click handler pushes reviews/ with no query. Checked by tracing the click handler and by test_open_reviews_are_listed_first_and_each_box_changes_the_list_and_the_address.

files.note: Fixed column widths, the stack spacing, the phone layout, and no underlines in the table.

checks.text: Every row stands in its own table body unless it belongs to a stack, so this one rule draws a divider under each lone row and under each stack's last row.
At phone width .date hides the col, the header, and every cell of the Updated column together. The review checked this by reading the CSS, not in a browser.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Node-driven tests of the boxes and the address, plus a build-level stack-order test.
intro: ReviewsViewTests runs the compiled showReviews under Node against a stub DOM and records the list and the address after each box change. A new build-level test in SiteContentTests covers a stack whose numbers run against its order, and the sidebar tests follow the rules to their new shared selectors.

checks.text: Walks the boxes through Closed on, Open off, Closed off, Open on, and expects the addresses /reviews/#top, ?state=open,closed#top, ?state=closed#top, ?state=#top, then /reviews/#top again, with the stack of 9, 10, and 11 kept together when 9 is merged and hidden.
Pull request 35 sits on 40 and 50 on 35, so the expected order is 40, 35, 50 by what sits on what, then the lone 41 and 38.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The CLI reference and the summary format describe the new index.
intro: docs/cli.md describes the boxes, the address, and the row look. It also stops saying a stack's base must be an open pull request, because stack_bases never checks the state of the pull request beneath. The summary format in skills/summarize-pr/format.md says where name still appears now that the index shows titles.

checks.text: The revised entry drops the clause saying the page uses name when the pull request has no title. pr_title and the summary page's header still fall back that way, so a reader of this file no longer learns that name can title the page. Consider keeping "and use name only when that title is empty".
